message.content:
The original square has area \(49\), so its side length is

\[
\sqrt{49}=7.
\]

Folding one pair of opposite corners together creates a crease along the other diagonal of the square. When unfolded, this diagonal divides the square into two congruent right isosceles triangles.

Each triangle has legs of length \(7\), and its hypotenuse is the square’s diagonal:

\[
\sqrt{7^2+7^2}=7\sqrt{2}.
\]

So the perimeter of one triangle is

\[
7+7+7\sqrt{2}=14+7\sqrt{2}.
\]

The answer is \(14+7\sqrt{2}\).
